reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that social influence acts as a mean-field force pulling agents toward the arithmetic mean, but the true center of the distribution is the geometric mean. This mismatch causes systematic drift away from truth even when individual agents start close. The model assumes log-normality of opinions, which implies that the geometric mean is more robust to skew than the arithmetic mean. In GSE, this translates into enforcing log-space aggregation to prevent distortion caused by social influence. The key failure mode occurs when all sub-models become correlated through shared signals, reducing diversity without improving accuracy. Thus, GSE must monitor forecast variance and enforce independence among components. The system also requires a diversity metric to detect when consensus is forming too quickly, indicating possible herding behavior. The model's validation shows that arithmetic mean performs poorly compared to geometric mean in skewed environments, supporting the use of log-space aggregation in GSI.
